images.title: Bottles counted in fourths
images.purpose: Show that 3 3/4 bottles is 4 + 4 + 4 + 3 = 15 cups of 1/4, so 3 3/4 = 15/4.
images.composition: Four identical bottles in a row with even spacing, two short count lines under them, and one equation centred below.
images.exact_structure: Four identical simple bottles: a tall rectangle body with a small plain neck. Each body is split by thin grey #6B7280 lines into exactly 4 equal horizontal parts. First 3 bottles: all 4 parts filled teal #0072B2. Fourth bottle: the bottom 3 parts filled amber #E69F00, the top part empty. Under the first 3 bottles, one count; under the row, one sum; below it, one equation in reddish purple #CC79A7. Exactly 4 bottles, 15 filled parts.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec

images.takeaway: Turn each whole into 4 fourths, then add the fourths left: 15/4.
images.description: Three full teal bottles of 4 fourths and one bottle with 3 amber fourths; 3 bottles make 12 fourths, 12 + 3 = 15 fourths, and 3 3/4 = 15/4 sits below.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to count the filled parts bottle by bottle and say the total as fifteen fourths.

image_decisions.why: Counting fourths in each bottle turns the mixed number back into a fraction in one picture.
